After rolling out iOS 26.6, iPadOS 26.6 and related software updates, Apple has detailed the large number of security patches included in today's new system versions.

Apple's security updates in iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 affect iPhone and iPad in a number of ways

iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 collectively provide over 75 security patches for iPhone and iPad, covering multiple layers of the system.

More specifically, Apple's security advisory lists 78 vulnerability entries, involving 87 separate CVE identifiers. Some entries correspond to more than one CVE, which is why the number of CVEs is higher.

Apple has not indicated that any of the vulnerabilities patched in iOS 26.6 have been exploited in malicious attacks.

Within Apple's long list, several patches deserve particular attention:

  • A vulnerability in MediaRemote could allow an app to gain root privileges.
  • A vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder could allow an app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges.
  • Vulnerabilities in Game Center and libc could allow a malicious app to escape the sandbox.
  • A vulnerability in CloudAttestation could allow a malicious app to bypass code signing restrictions.
  • A vulnerability in ImageIO could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a specially crafted malicious image.
  • Three vulnerabilities in SceneKit could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing specially crafted malicious files.
  • An accessibility issue could cause sensitive data in iPhone Mirroring output to be disclosed to a person with physical access.
  • A vulnerability in Contacts could allow an app to add contacts without user authorisation.

Kernel, WebKit and Wi-Fi patches

Apple has also patched around a dozen kernel vulnerabilities. Potential impacts include corrupting or writing to kernel memory, leaking kernel memory, bypassing network filtering, and causing the system to terminate unexpectedly.

WebKit has also received a large number of patches. These vulnerabilities could lead to process memory leaks, disclosure of whether a user has visited a particular link, allowing UI spoofing, breaching iframe sandbox rules, allowing apps to read files outside the sandbox, or causing Safari to crash.

Another Wi-Fi vulnerability could allow a nearby attacker to corrupt process memory.

After the 78 documented security patches, Apple has an additional "Additional Recognition" section listing 12 entries.

These entries thank researchers for their assistance, but are not separate security patches and have not been assigned additional CVE identifiers.

The full patch list and researcher acknowledgements have been published on Apple's website.

Security patches for Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV and Apple Vision Pro

Apple's newly released macOS Tahoe 26.6 security advisory lists 155 separate CVEs.

In addition to patches shared with iPhone and iPad, the Mac update also addresses multiple vulnerabilities, including ones that could allow an app to gain root privileges, escape the sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper checks or privacy preferences, and access protected data.

Apple has also released security updates for older versions of macOS today, but these have not been included in this article's statistics.

Apple has also published patch contents for watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6 and visionOS 26.6. After excluding overlapping items across platforms, the latest updates collectively address 194 separate CVEs.

Apple previously revealed that, in response to AI-driven attack tools, iOS 26.5.2 released last month had accelerated the deployment of multiple security patches.
